question.text: 'Lotus Capital AIF' has a waterfall: 8% hurdle (LPs get 8% IRR first), 100% GP catch-up, then 80/20 carry. Deal IRR on a single exit is 14%. On INR 100 crore realised profit above LP capital, roughly how does the LP/GP split work AT CATCH-UP stage?

answer.text: LP gets first ~8% IRR layer; then GP catches-up to 20% of profits; then 80/20 split on the remainder.
GP gets first 20% of profits flat regardless of hurdle.
LP gets 100% of profits up to 20% IRR.

explanation.text: The Logic: With 8% hurdle + 100% catch-up + 80/20 thereafter: LPs first receive distributions up to 8% IRR; then the GP receives 100% of subsequent distributions until total GP share = 20% of cumulative profits including hurdle; residual is split 80/20 LP/GP. This is the classic European-style waterfall for Cat I/II. The Trap: GP-first-20% ignores the hurdle. LP-100%-up-to-20% ignores catch-up. 50/50 is fabricated. Cross-Exam Context: XIX-C and Ch 6 Fee Structure go deep on waterfalls. XIX-D tests the mechanics at fund level, XIX-A at LP-return level. Manager's Pro-Tip: Draft the catch-up as 100% or 80/20 catch-up explicitly - ambiguity on catch-up speed is the most common waterfall dispute.
